name: Pharmaceuticals
one_liner: Pharma companies discover, develop and sell drugs, spending heavily on risky R&D and earning high margins during a limited patent-protected window before generics or biosimilars arrive.
how_it_makes_money: Branded drugs sell at premium prices while protected by patents and exclusivity, generating most industry profit. Net revenue is list price minus rebates and discounts negotiated with PBMs, insurers and government programs; generic makers compete on low cost and volume.
revenue_formula: Drug revenue = treated patients × days of therapy × net price
Treated patients = disease prevalence × diagnosis rate × treatment rate × market share
Net price = list price - rebates, discounts and government concessions
cost_structure: R&D: often roughly 15-25% of revenue for large pharma, including many failed programs
Selling, general and administrative: sales reps, marketing, market access
Cost of goods sold: manufacturing, relatively low for small molecules
Licensing and acquisitions: in-licensed assets, milestones and royalties
margins: Large branded pharma typically earns high gross margins (often ~70-80%) and strong operating margins, while generics run much thinner; the spread depends on patent protection, pipeline productivity and pricing pressure.

key_metrics.name: Probability of technical and regulatory success (PTRS)
key_metrics.what: Likelihood a candidate reaches approval; drives risk-adjusted pipeline value.

key_metrics.name: Risk-adjusted NPV (rNPV)
key_metrics.what: Value of a drug program weighted by phase success odds; the standard asset valuation tool.

key_metrics.name: Peak sales
key_metrics.what: Expected maximum annual revenue of a drug; frames commercial potential.

key_metrics.name: Gross-to-net discount
key_metrics.what: Gap between list and net price; shows rebate and pricing pressure.

key_metrics.name: Loss of exclusivity (LOE) exposure
key_metrics.what: Revenue facing generic or biosimilar competition soon; the 'patent cliff' risk.

key_metrics.name: R&D as % of sales
key_metrics.what: Research intensity; balanced against pipeline output.
